16-12-2023 (Clause 31) AWARD 1.

As per the facts of present case, in the intervening night of 1920/05/2014 deceased Ram Niwas S/O Brij Singh, alongwith his four coemployees was going to refill cash in ATMs machine in Punhana,Mewat, Haryana in the offending vehicle No.HR55T1080 being driven by its driver/respondent No.1.
It is alleged that the offending vehicle was driven at a very high speed in rash, negligent and by neglecting the traffic rules.
The driver of offending vehicle did not bother the request of passengers to drive carefully.

When they reached near village Bhuryakhi, Punhana,
Mewat, Haryana, the driver/ respondent No.1 lost his control over the offending vehicle and said vehicle fell into a Canal.
As a result of which, the deceased alongwith three cotravelers drowned into water in the Canal.
The deceased was taken to Govt Hospital,Mandi Khera, Punahana, Mewat where concerned Doctor declared him brought dead.
The Post Mortem on the body of deceased Ram Niwas was conducted in the aforesaid hospital.
The present case pertains to the death of Sh Ram Niwas.
2. It is contended that said accident took place, due to use of offending vehicle by Bir Singh in negligent manner who has been impleaded as respondent no. 1.
The owner of offending vehicle is M/S Secure Value India Ltd and it is impleaded as respondent no. 2.
As the said vehicle was insured with Magma HDI General Insurance Company Ltd., hence it is impleaded as respondent no. 3 in the present case.

sentences.text: By the present petition, the petitioners are claiming a sum of Rs. 80,00,000/ (Rupees Eighty Lacs Only) from respondents as compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 has not filed any reply/W.S to the petition.
4. The respondent No. 2 has filed its W.S stating therein that respondent No.1 /driver of offending vehicle was not driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.

Hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

6. After completion of the pleadings, following issues were framed on 16.08.2016 :
(i) Whether Ram Niwas sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 19 20/05/2014 due to use and involvement of vehicle ( Truck) No. HR55T1080 by R.1 ?

OPP. 
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
(iii) Relief.

However the present petition as well as connected matter bearing No. MACP No.626/16 Arita Vs Bir Singh pertains to same accident hence both the petitions were taken together.

sentences.text: As some of the documents of the present petition are also place in the connected matter Arita Vs Bir Singh but petition bearing No. MACP No.626/16 Arita Vs Bir Singh was dismissed in default vide order dated 20.11.2019.
The Ld Predecessor during the course of inquiry has also summoned the aforesaid file from the record room to arrive at conclusion to award just and reasonable compensation to the victims.
8. I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondents No.1 to 3.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission made by them and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE NO. 1: (i) (i) Whether Ram Niwas sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 1920/05/2014 due to use and involvement of vehicle (
Truck) No. HR55T1080 by R.1 ? OPP.
9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

To prove this fact petitioners have examined PW1 Smt Mindra Devi who deposed that her husband Ram Niwas had died on 19 20/05/2014 in a road accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing No.
HR55T1080 by respondent No.1 when was travelling in the aforesaid vehicle for loading cash in ATM Machines at Punhana.
10. Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company has argued that no witness has been produced by the petitioners to prove that the offending vehicle was being driven by R.1 in rash and negligent manner.

11. On the other hand, Ld Counsel for the petitioner has argued that a certified copy of charge sheet is there on record in which R.1 Bir Singh has been made as an accused U/S 279/304A IPC which is sufficient to prove the fact of rash and negligent driving by R.1.

6 12.
Having considered the submission of Ld Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company.
It is worth mention here some judgments of Hon'ble Superior Court.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Ors Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530 has held that the " Claim Tribunal has to decide the negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim petition".
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Pushpa Rana & Ors 2008 (101) DRJ 645 the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard Ld Counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Meena Variyal; 2007(5) SCALE 269. ( LQ/SC/2007/437).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (I) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle.

(ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach at the conclusion that driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver."

14. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Som Dutt Sharma MAC App 758/2015 & CP Appl 22387/2015 has also held that to determine the rash and negligent, the criminal case record is sufficient to proof to reach to the conclusion that driver was negligent.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Som Dutt Sharma MAC App 758/2015 & CP Appl 22387/2015
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
The fact that Sh. Ram Niwas died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle No.HR55T 1080 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh. Ram Mehar Gupta.
16.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Ram Niwas died in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle No.HR55T1080.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
17.
The Petitioner no.1 is the wife , petitioner 2 and 3 are sons, while petitioner No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased, as such LRs of victim.

7 18.
The first argument of Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company is that the insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation as insurance policy does not cover the deceased/victim Ram Niwas.
19. On perusal.

Admittedly, the deceased was an employee with M/S Secure Value India Ltd, 96,
Phase1, Udyog Vihar, Gurgaon, Haryana as a security person.
It is not denied that the offending vehicle was not insured with the insurance company, R.3.
It is also not denied by R.3 that the offending vehicle used to carry cash for filling up the cash in ATM Machines.
The victim being a security person usually traveled in the offending vehicle to give security to the Van.

Even otherwise,
an award was passed in a Claim Petition No.71 in case titled as Laxmi Devi & ors Vs Bir Singh & Ors decided by MACT, Gurgaon in which the same type of issue has also been adjudicated and employees were considered being coveredunder the insurance policy.

entities.text: Laxmi Devi & ors Vs Bir Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Insurance company has deposited the award amount.
So this plea is not open to the Insurance company that victim/ Ram Niwas cannot be termed third party.
This this submission of Ld Counsel for the insurance company is not sustainable and same is discarded.
20. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
PW1 Mindra Devi , has deposed that her husband was 44 years of age at the time of accident.
She has deposed that at the time of accident, the deceased was working as Gunman with Secure Value India Ltd and earning Rs. 32,556/ p.m
His earning would have been increasing on day to day basis, if he could have alive.
Ld Counsel for the petitioner also submits that R.2 has also admitted in his W.S that salary of victim/deceased was Rs.32,556/ per month.
But the submission of Ld Counsel for the petitioner is contrary to the documents and as such the oral submission of Ld Counsel can not be subsists if documentary evidence is there on record.
In this case R.2 has issued a salary certificate Ex PW1/5 (Colly )in which gross monthly income of victim was shown as 14,330/.

The testimony of PW1 also cannot be considered against the document Ex PW1/5.
21.

On perusal of Ex PW1/5, it denotes gross monthly salary of Rs.14,330/ So by deducting the medical allowance and Conveyance allowances which are personal expenses of victim and after adding annual bonus of Rs.6,667/ ( monthly of which is Rs. 556/ in lumbsum).
The monthly income for the purpose of computation of compensation is taken as Rs.12,836/ p.m.
No tax have been deducted on the salary of victim.

22.And as per the judgment in the case Rajesh Vs Rajbir Singh 2013 ACJ 1403 SC and in others cases Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that the net income of the deceased is to be counted after adding future benefit @ 30%.

entities.text: Rajesh Vs Rajbir Singh 2013 ACJ 1403 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are five LRs of victim so he ( deceased) is presumed to be spending 1/4th of his income on his personal expenses.

So the loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs. 12,515.10/ (12,836/ +3,850.80/  6,618.75/) per month.
23.
The age of the deceased was 44 years at the time of accident.
To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 14 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 21,02,536.80 ( 12,515.10/ x 12 x 14. ).
This amount of Rs.21,02,536.80/ is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

8 24.

Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioners no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs. 2,20,000/ (Rs. 44,000/ each to all the petitioners) for loss of consortium, making a total sum of compensation as Rs.23,56,536.80/

The Detail of the whole award amount is: i. Loss of dependency Rs. 21,02,536.80/ ii. Funeral expenses Rs. 17,000/ iii. Loss of Estate Rs. 17,000/ v. Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/ to each petitioner Rs. 2,20,000/ Total Rs. 23,56,536.80/
25.
Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to negligent parking of offending veicle by the respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the Respondent no.3 on the date of accident.

Moreover, the evidence of the petitioner fully supports his case, therefore, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from Respondent no.3 ISSUE NO.3 (RELIEF)
26.
Petition in hands is allowed.

Respondent no.3 is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 23,56,536.80/ (
Round of to Rs.23,56,540/) alongwith interest @ 7.5% p.a from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 08.01.2015 till the date of compliance i.e., 17.12.2023.

Amount of interim compensation (if any)
be deducted from this amount.
Thereafter interest @ 12% p.a for delayed payment.

The awarded amount shall remain as tax free in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case in R/Special Civil Application No.4800 of 2021 titled The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS) decided on 05.04.2022 27.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The driver of offending vehicle did not bother the request of passengers to drive carefully.
When they reached near village Bhuryakhi, Punhana,
Mewat, Haryana, the driver/ respondent No.1 lost his control over the offending vehicle and said vehicle fell into a Canal.
As a result of which, the deceased alongwith three cotravelers drowned into water in the Canal.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Ors Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530 has held that the " Claim Tribunal has to decide the negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim petition".
13.
In National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Pushpa Rana & Ors 2008 (101) DRJ 645 the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard Ld Counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Meena Variyal; 2007(5) SCALE 269. ( LQ/SC/2007/437).
14. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Som Dutt Sharma MAC App 758/2015 & CP Appl 22387/2015 has also held that to determine the rash and negligent, the criminal case record is sufficient to proof to reach to the conclusion that driver was negligent.
15. It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.
Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle No.HR55T 1080 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh. Ram Mehar Gupta.
16.
It is also not denied by R.3 that the offending vehicle used to carry cash for filling up the cash in ATM Machines.
The victim being a security person usually traveled in the offending vehicle to give security to the Van.
Even otherwise,
an award was passed in a Claim Petition No.71 in case titled as Laxmi Devi & ors Vs Bir Singh & Ors decided by MACT, Gurgaon in which the same type of issue has also been adjudicated and employees were considered being coveredunder the insurance policy.
The Insurance company has deposited the award amount.
So the loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs. 12,515.10/ (12,836/ +3,850.80/  6,618.75/) per month.
23.
The age of the deceased was 44 years at the time of accident.
To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 14 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 21,02,536.80 ( 12,515.10/ x 12 x 14. ).
This amount of Rs.21,02,536.80/ is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.
However, the petitioner has made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
